criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines (~160 chars, inside the 210 cutoff) name RED FLAG-Alaska 26-2, June 12, Donnelly Drop Zone, troop/aircraft counts, five nations. 'Alaska wasn't the backdrop. It was the test.' delivers the stake. Short of 10 because the capital consequence is hinted, not named, in the hook.

criteria.name: Industry relevance
criteria.notes: Every paragraph pairs an AK event with a named business consequence (JPARC doctrine becomes procurement spec; RFLP June 29 + GVEA grid-cost; GCI reseller economics). Minor: GCI paragraph omits the BEAD routing angle.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics in nearly every sentence (units, bases, dates, communities, partner nations). Short of 10 only because no dollar figures appear (RFLP has no published ceiling; GCI deal size unverified).

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: All three lead stories map to verified high-confidence entries, each 2+ sources (DVIDS x3; Alaska's News Source + News-Miner; Telecompetitor + Broadband Breakfast). Stak handled as background with attribution. Minor: Stak out-of-window.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, position-taking, structural. No banned phrases; 'leverage' used as noun. GCI lines slightly telegraphic. On-voice with post_001.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Four paragraphs + closing question, 3-5 sentences each. 430 words, 2,749 chars. Second paragraph densest but scannable.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Specific, debatable, tied to the test-bed vs program-capture tension and the RED FLAG / RFLP decision cycle. Could name the specific mechanism to demand.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: Reader can name the June 29 RFLP deadline, JPARC doctrine venue, GCI/Starlink BEAD signal, and Stak comment period as revisit triggers.

one_sentence_fix: Sharpen the closing question by naming a specific mechanism Alaska should demand (IP ownership, data-sovereignty terms in the RFLP, or ANC task-order preference) rather than the open-ended 'what should it demand in return.'
